subject: Competitive replacement: savings structure and transition milestones
messages:
From: Ethan Myers <ethan@cloudline.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Cloudline Procurement <procurement@cloudline.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Exploring a switch — pricing gap and timeline

Karthik / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran the internal econ model and there9s a clear delta between what our incumbent is offering (18 months of effective credits stacked over a 3-year term) and Redwood9s published pricing. We like Redwood9s latency and the dedicated capacity controls, but procurement needs a concrete migration package to justify the move.

Key asks from our side:
- Can Redwood match the incumbent9s effective ARR reduction (we estimate ~22% PV impact over 3 years)?
- What migration credits, ramp guarantees, or technical onboarding support can you commit to?
- Any minimum term or commit you9d need from Cloudline?

We9re talking to procurement and engineering in parallel — Olivia (copied) is coordinating the procurement side. Hoping to get a figure and a short slide we can take to the exec committee by next Tues (28th).

Ethan

--
Ethan Myers

Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring a switch — pricing gap and timeline

Ethan — thanks for the clear asks. High level: we9re prepared to put forward a targeted retention/migration package that balances upfront onboarding cost and the long-term unit economics that Redwood needs to preserve. I9ve looped in Marissa and Lauren to size credits and ramp terms; Sean can speak to any SLA or dedicated pool availability constraints for your region.

Immediate next steps I propose:
1) Marissa to draft a structured counteroffer (credits + term + optional prepay) and an annotated migration milestone schedule.
2) We9ll attach a concise cost comparison spreadsheet you can use with procurement.
3) If that looks ok, schedule a 30-min exec Q&A with our Head of Revenue (optional) before your 28th meeting.

We9ll aim to get a first pass to you by end of day Wednesday (22nd). Appreciate the timeline — we9ll prioritize.

Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ethan Myers <ethan@cloudline.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Competitive package — draft proposal and migration sketch

Karthik / Ethan — attaching a compact proposal and a migration milestone sketch. High-level summary below.

Proposal (first pass):
- Term/Commit: 24 months, with optional 12-month auto-extension.
- Economic match: We9re offering an upfront onboarding credit equal to 20% of Year 1 committed spend, plus a 6-month runway credit applied to token usage (this effectively front-loads ~18% of Year 1 spend). The combination aims to close the 22% PV gap you referenced without undermining long-run pricing.
- Ramp guarantee: Dedicated capacity reserved for 90 days post-go-live with a rollback option if performance SLOs (p95 latency) are not met.
- Professional Services: 5 days of complimentary integration support; additional days available at a discounted PS rate.
- Migration milestones: pilot (2 weeks) -> staged rollout (4 weeks) -> full cutover target (8 weeks). We can compress for a paid accelerated path.

Attachments: cloudline_competitive_analysis_v2.xlsx (tabbed econ scenarios) and migration_milestones_sketch.pdf (timeline + owners).

Questions for procurement: what9s the incumbent9s exact cash-back / credit structuring? Is the incumbent providing usage credits, or are they offering a pure discount on list? We structured ours as credits because it9s auditable and helps with your cost recognition.

Ethan — if you want us to tighten the numbers this morning, tell us the target PV difference you need closed and Marissa will adjust.

Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: Olivia Park <olivia@cloudline.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Ethan Myers <ethan@cloudline.com>, Cloudline Procurement <procurement@cloudline.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Competitive package — draft proposal and migration sketch

Thanks — the structure is helpful. A few clarifications before we take this to the execs: 

1) Payment timing: Can the onboarding credit be applied as a dollar-for-dollar offset in the first quarter invoice rather than amortized over the year? Our CFO prefers simpler recognition.
2) Pilot terms: the pilot needs an explicit rollback clause and a short SLA credit if performance dips during staged rollout.
3) We9d like an additional 30 days of complimentary support (total 35 days) tied to specific onboarding milestones; is that possible?

If you can accommodate (1) as a billing offset and (3) the extra 30 days, we9re close to greenlighting the terms for exec review. Also — can you provide a brief one-slide summary we can hand off to our CFO that shows net PV impact vs incumbent?

Olivia

--
Olivia Park
Procurement Manager, Cloudline Systems
olivia@cloudline.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia@cloudline.com>, Ethan Myers <ethan@cloudline.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Sep 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Competitive package — draft proposal and migration sketch

Olivia / Ethan — appreciate the quick review and clear asks. We can accommodate the three items with the following confirmations: 

1) Billing offset: onboarding credit applied as a dollar-for-dollar invoice credit in Q1 (no amortization) — confirmed.
2) Pilot SLA credit: we9ll add a clause: if p95 latency exceeds the agreed threshold for more than 3 cumulative hours during staged rollout, Redwood will issue a pro-rated usage credit for that week (details in contract).
3) Additional support days: we can increase complimentary PS to 35 days tied to milestone sign-offs (pilot acceptance + staged rollout completion).

Updated economic summary (high level):
- 24-month term.
- Upfront onboarding invoice credit = 20% of Year 1 committed spend, applied in Q1.
- 6-month usage runway credit applied token-for-token after onboarding credit is used.
- 35 days of complimentary integration support.
- Reserved dedicated capacity for 90 days post-go-live.

Next steps: I9ll send a one-slide PV comparison and a redline-friendly term sheet. If this looks good, Marissa will produce a DocuSign for a standard 24-month MSA with the migration addendum. Can we book 30 minutes tomorrow (24th) at 3pm PT for final Q&A?

Karthik
